intent_summary: Review the landed P8 (reports and output) code: 10 fixed report types generated directly via ReportLab plus a custom report builder executed asynchronously through ARQ. Both /report/generate and /report-builder/execute return 202 with a task_id; terminal state lives in report_files.status and report_execution_logs.status; a reclaimer judges dead tasks FAILED rather than deleting rows, because the log is an audit table. The review focus is async task lifecycle correctness (submit / retry / reclaim), project-level data isolation, and migration-to-ORM consistency.

peer.note: No cross-model route exists on this host; the adversarial perspective is covered by the in-process adversarial reviewer.

batch.cap_note: 8 P0/P1 survive, which is exactly the normal cap of eight; no expansion was needed and the batch is not split.

findings.title: Fixed-10 report export has no project isolation: join rows are unfiltered and record_ids ownership is never checked
findings.why_it_matters: Verified in source, three linked gaps on the fixed-10-types path only. (1) `_fetch_join_rows` (pcs-backend/app/services/report/report_service.py:163-177) takes no `scope` argument and adds no project predicate: it selects every row of the joined source whose join key matches, so a main-source row belonging to project A pulls in join-source rows belonging to project B. (2) `_filter_spec` (:139-160) builds the only predicate on the main source and it is an `IN` over `record_ids` -- the primary key list from the request body; nothing checks that those ids belong to `body.project_id`. (3) `POST /report/generate` (pcs-backend/app/api/v1/report.py:135-186) calls `check_project_access_or_404` on `body.project_id` (:143) and then hands `body.record_ids` straight to the queue (:186), so the access check validates a project id that never reaches the query. The intended pattern exists 40 lines away in `builder_service._fetch_join_rows_with_scope` (pcs-backend/app/services/report/builder_service.py:99-134), which takes `scope` and ANDs `_attr(source, "project_id") == scope` -- bug-162 fixed only that path. Consequence: an authenticated user who knows or guesses record UUIDs from another project exports another project's rows through a supported endpoint. Tests do not cover this: tests/services/report/test_join_project_scope.py exercises only `builder_service.execute_definition`.
findings.first_evidence: pcs-backend/app/services/report/report_service.py:107 — `rows_by_source[extra] = await _fetch_join_rows(db, source=extra, join_field=b_key, keys=[...])` with no `scope=` argument.
evidence: pcs-backend/app/services/report/report_service.py:107 — `rows_by_source[extra] = await _fetch_join_rows(db, source=extra, join_field=b_key, keys=[...])` with no `scope=` argument.
pcs-backend/app/services/report/report_service.py:163 — `_fetch_join_rows` signature accepts only `source`, `join_field`, `keys`; no project scoping.
Compare: pcs-backend/app/services/report/builder_service.py:2239 — same join-source path explicitly ANDs `_attr(source, 'project_id') == scope` and justifies it as '越权边界, 不能与 user conditions 合并'.

Trigger: caller POSTs `/report/generate` with `project_id=A` and `record_ids=[<UUID from project B>]`; `/report/generate` only runs `check_project_access_or_404` on project_id, not on individual record ids.

pcs-backend/app/services/report/report_service.py:4819-4844 — `collect()` builds `stmt = build_select(...) .where(apply_filters(_filter_spec(spec, record_ids)))` with no project_id clause; `_filter_spec()` returns only the IN(record_ids) condition.

pcs-backend/app/services/report/builder_service.py:2310-2319 — by contrast, `execute_definition` adds an explicit `{"operator":"EQ","source":primary,"field":_project_field(primary),"value":scope}` condition, with a docstring calling this a hard boundary: "**不能默认全库查询** —— 那会把别的项目的数据一起导出去".
pcs-backend/app/api/v1/report.py:628-631 — endpoint calls `check_project_access_or_404(body.project_id)` but never re-uses that project_id in the SQL path.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a `scope: uuid.UUID | None` parameter to `_fetch_join_rows` and to `collect`; thread `project_id` through from the endpoint. In the batched IN query, mirror builder_service's guard: if the source exposes a project_id column, AND `project_id == scope`; if not (e.g. SUPPLIERS), keep current behavior. Also validate at the endpoint that every UUID in `body.record_ids` resolves to a row whose `project_id` matches `body.project_id` (or NULL), with `check_project_access_or_404` per row.

findings.title: Reclaim cron never commits -- the stale-task reclaimer is silently inert
findings.why_it_matters: Verified in source: `reclaim_stale_tasks` (pcs-backend/app/workers/report_tasks.py:217-251) and `reclaim_stale_execution_logs` (:263-308) end with `await db.flush()` (:249, :307) and no commit; the last `commit()` in the whole module is at :203, inside `generate_report_task`. The cron entry `reclaim_stale_report_tasks(ctx)` (:311-328) obtains its session through `_ctx_session(ctx)` (:323,:331-338), which calls the session factory and never commits or closes. The module docstring (:15-26) states every state change in this module must commit and explicitly exempts reclaim -- the exemption is the bug. Consequence: every FAILED rewrite and every REPORT_FAILED audit row the reclaimer writes is rolled back when the session is released, so a crashed ARQ worker leaves report_files stuck in PENDING and report_execution_logs stuck in QUEUED/RUNNING forever; the status endpoints the frontend polls report a hang that never resolves. The two reviewers describe the same defect from the same file and merge into one finding.
evidence: pcs-backend/app/workers/report_tasks.py:249 — `await db.flush()` inside `reclaim_stale_tasks` (no commit before return).
pcs-backend/app/workers/report_tasks.py:307 — `await db.flush()` inside `reclaim_stale_execution_logs` (no commit before return).
Module docstring at pcs-backend/app/workers/report_tasks.py:25-32: 每次状态变更必须 commit 与实际函数不符 — reclaim 是显豁。
Trigger: cron `reclaim-stale-report-tasks` fires at HH:03:00 and HH:33:00 via `WorkerSettings.cron_jobs`; each invocation calls `_ctx_session(ctx)` which only opens a session and never closes it.

pcs-backend/app/workers/report_tasks.py:323-328 — `db: AsyncSession = _ctx_session(ctx)` / `await reclaim_stale_tasks(db, older_than_minutes=STALE_MINUTES)` / `await reclaim_stale_execution_logs(db, older_than_minutes=STALE_MINUTES)` — no `commit()`, no `close()` anywhere in the function.

pcs-backend/app/workers/report_tasks.py:249 — `    await db.flush()` (end of reclaim_stale_tasks); pcs-backend/app/workers/report_tasks.py:307 — `    await db.flush()` (end of reclaim_stale_execution_logs). Both rely on a caller that never commits.
pcs-backend/app/db/session.py:71-85 — `get_async_session_factory` builds a plain `async_sessionmaker` with no autocommit; there is no ambient commit hook that could rescue the flush.

tests/workers/test_report_tasks.py:306 — `n = await reclaim_stale_tasks(db, older_than_minutes=15)` — the tests pass the fixture session directly and never exercise the cron wrapper, so the missing commit is invisible to CI.

Contrast with the task bodies, which do commit explicitly and are tested for it: report_tasks.py:172 `            await db.commit()`, and tests/workers/test_report_tasks.py:381 `test_failure_state_is_committed_not_just_left_in_the_session`.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `await db.commit()` at the end of `reclaim_stale_tasks` (line 249) and `reclaim_stale_execution_logs` (line 307), and switch the cron entry to use `session_scope(ctx)` (the helper added in worker.py) so the session is also guaranteed to close cleanly. Add a `test_reclaim_persists_after_session_close` that calls the function against one session, commits/closes, then re-opens a fresh session and asserts the row state (and audit row) actually landed in the DB.

findings.title: Builder enqueues the ARQ job before committing its execution-log row
findings.why_it_matters: Verified in source: `execute_definition_endpoint` calls `arq_queue.enqueue_definition_execution(...)` at :328, adds the `ReportExecutionLog` row at :348, and only commits at :368. Three windows: the worker can finish and call `_link_report_file` before the row exists, so the audit row's `report_file_id` backfill is lost and the polling endpoint `/report-builder/executions/{task_id}` answers 404 for a job that already produced a file; if the endpoint then fails before :368, the file exists with no audit row at all. The fixed-10 endpoint gets this right on purpose -- pcs-backend/app/api/v1/report.py:157-166 builds the PENDING row and commits before enqueueing -- so the two endpoints in the same feature contradict each other.
evidence: pcs-backend/app/api/v1/report_builder.py:328: `    task_id = await arq_queue.enqueue_definition_execution(` (enqueue happens first)
pcs-backend/app/api/v1/report_builder.py:348: `    db.add(ReportExecutionLog(` (row created second) with `:368: await db.commit()` after it.

pcs-backend/app/workers/report_builder_tasks.py:245-250: `    await db.execute(update(ReportExecutionLog).where(ReportExecutionLog.task_id == task_id).values(report_file_id=report_file_id))` -- UPDATE-only, no row-count check, no upsert.
pcs-backend/app/api/v1/report_builder.py:328 — `    task_id = await arq_queue.enqueue_definition_execution(` — the job is on the queue before the log row exists.
pcs-backend/app/api/v1/report_builder.py:368 — `    await db.commit()      # 端点负责 commit（与本仓其它写端点一致）` — the log row (added at line 348) is only durable here, after the enqueue.

pcs-backend/app/workers/report_builder_tasks.py:75-76 — `        task_row = (await db.execute(_sel(_Log).where(` / `            _Log.task_id == job_id))).scalar_one_or_none()` — a miss here makes both the RUNNING update and the later backfill no-ops.

pcs-backend/app/workers/report_builder_tasks.py:229 — `    await _link_report_file(db, task_id=task_id, report_file_id=row.report_file_id)` — the UPDATE at 247-250 silently affects 0 rows; there is no rowcount check.

Parallel pattern already in this diff: pcs-backend/app/api/v1/report.py:161 `    task_id = uuid.uuid4().hex` … :189 `_job_id=task_id,` — the generate endpoint commits the PENDING row *before* enqueueing.
`enqueue_definition_execution` (arq_queue.py:81-85) does not forward a `_job_id`, so the task id cannot currently be chosen by the caller on this path.
findings.suggested_fix: Reorder `execute_definition_endpoint` so the `db.add(ReportExecutionLog(...))` + `await db.commit()` precede `arq_queue.enqueue_definition_execution(...)`, and pass the endpoint-chosen task_id into the enqueue (mirroring what `/report/generate` already does at report.py:161-190 with `_job_id=task_id`). Additionally make `_link_report_file` raise or retry when its UPDATE matches zero rows, so this class of silent loss surfaces instead of degrading into a client-side timeout.

findings.title: Printed QR codes carry no signature, so /report/verify rejects every scan with 403
findings.why_it_matters: Verified in source, and the gap is end-to-end: `build_qr_payload` (pcs-backend/app/services/report/qr.py:25-43) emits `{verify_base_url}/api/v1/report/verify/{report_id}#...` with no `sig` and no `exp` query parameter, and grepping the whole backend finds no other producer -- `hmac` appears only in the verifier. `_check_sig` (pcs-backend/app/api/v1/report.py:97-110) requires both: `sig` must equal HMAC-SHA256(secret, f"{report_file_id}:{exp}") and `exp` must be in the future, so with the signature absent it raises 403 '签名无效' on every request. The endpoint module docstring (:25) specifies the signature contract, and migration-side settings define `report_verify_secret`; only the producer is missing. Field verification -- scanning a printed report to confirm it against the stored hash -- cannot succeed today.
findings.first_evidence: pcs-backend/app/services/report/report_service.py:220 — `                          qr_payload=None, assumed_fields=[], context=ctx)` — the render call hardcodes None, so renderer_pdf.py:256 `    if qr_payload:` is never true.
evidence: pcs-backend/app/services/report/report_service.py:220 — `                          qr_payload=None, assumed_fields=[], context=ctx)` — the render call hardcodes None, so renderer_pdf.py:256 `    if qr_payload:` is never true.
grep for `build_qr_payload` across the repo returns only its definition (qr.py:25) and tests/services/report/test_report_service.py — zero production callers.
grep for `report_verify_secret` returns app/api/v1/report.py:100 (verification), app/core/config.py:79/169/176 (config), tests/api/v1/test_report.py:49 (test-side signing) — no production signer.

pcs-backend/app/api/v1/report.py:107-110 — `    expect = hmac.new(secret.encode(), f"{report_file_id}:{exp}".encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()` / `    if not hmac.compare_digest(expect, sig or ""):` / `        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="签名无效")` — fail-closed, correct, and unsatisfiable for any URL a QR could carry.
pcs-backend/app/services/report/qr.py:43 — `    return (f"{verify_base_url.rstrip('/')}/api/v1/report/verify/{report_id}#"` — the payload builder emits no sig/exp query parameters.
findings.suggested_fix: Two coordinated changes, both in `report_service`. (1) Add a signer next to `qr.py` that mints the short-lived signature: `def sign_verify_url(*, report_file_id, exp) -> str` computing `hmac.new(settings.report_verify_secret.encode(), f"{report_file_id}:{exp}".encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()` — reuse the exact input format from `_check_sig` (report.py:107) rather than re-deriving it. (2) In `store_rendered`/`generate`, build `exp = int(now.timestamp()) + VERIFY_TTL_S` and pass a real payload through `_render_sync(..., qr_payload=build_qr_payload(..., verify_base_url=f"{base}/api/v1/report/verify/{row_id}?sig={sig}&exp={exp}"))` — note this requires the report_file_id, which today is only known *after* `_upsert_report_file`, so the ordering in `store_rendered` (render → hash → write → upsert) needs to become (upsert PENDING row → sign with its id → render → write). Because the signature is time-varying it must NOT feed `_content_hash`, or the determinism guarantee that `qr.py`'s docstring rests on (same content ⇒ same hash ⇒ dedup works) breaks; keep the hash over (blocks, style, output_format, ctx) as it is and let the QR vary. If signed URLs are genuinely deferred, delete `qr.py` and the `verify` route together rather than shipping a 403-by-construction endpoint.

findings.title: assemble()'s fixed batch_size=10000 hard-fails every definition whose MaxRows exceeds it, contradicting the 100,000-row promise
findings.why_it_matters: Verified in source: `query_engine.assemble` (:293-318) defaults `batch_size: int = 10000` and raises PcsError `REPORT_JOIN_TOO_LARGE` when the primary row count exceeds it. Both callers pass no `batch_size`: pcs-backend/app/services/report/builder_service.py:233 and pcs-backend/app/services/report/report_service.py:111. Meanwhile 100,000 is the promised ceiling in four places -- schemas/report_builder.py:139 and :165, definition_service.py:53 (`MAX_ROWS_CEILING`), and api/v1/report_builder.py:239. A user who saves a definition with max_rows between 10,001 and 100,000 passes validation and gets a hard 400 at execution time, which is the same class of bug the format whitelist docstring warns about ('saved fine, fails only at execution').
findings.first_evidence: pcs-backend/app/services/report/query_engine.py:313 — `    if len(base_rows) > batch_size:` with `batch_size: int = 10000` declared at query_engine.py:297 and raised as `REPORT_JOIN_TOO_LARGE` (400) at :317.
evidence: pcs-backend/app/services/report/query_engine.py:313 — `    if len(base_rows) > batch_size:` with `batch_size: int = 10000` declared at query_engine.py:297 and raised as `REPORT_JOIN_TOO_LARGE` (400) at :317.
pcs-backend/app/services/report/builder_service.py:233 — `    merged = qe.assemble(rows_by_source, join_keys, primary, fields_by_source)` — no `batch_size` argument, so the 10000 default applies.

pcs-backend/app/services/report/builder_service.py:193 — `    limit = temporary_max_rows or row.max_rows or 10000` and :222 `    main_rows = main_rows[:limit]` — `base_rows` reaching `assemble` has exactly `limit` rows, so `limit > 10000` deterministically trips the guard.

pcs-backend/app/schemas/report_builder.py:165 — `    max_rows: int = Field(default=10000, ge=1, le=100_000)` and pcs-backend/app/api/v1/report_builder.py:239 — `    max_rows: int | None = Field(default=None, ge=1, le=100_000)` both admit values the executor can never serve.
grep for `batch_size` across app/services/report and app/api/v1 returns only query_engine.py:297 (the default) and :313 (the check) — no caller anywhere raises or lowers it.
findings.suggested_fix: Thread the effective row limit into `assemble` from the one place that already knows it. In `builder_service.execute_definition`, the call at line 233 is `qe.assemble(rows_by_source, join_keys, primary, fields_by_source)`; change it to `qe.assemble(rows_by_source, join_keys, primary, fields_by_source, batch_size=limit)`, since `limit` (line 193) is `temporary_max_rows or row.max_rows or 10000` and `main_rows` has already been truncated to it at line 222 — so the check becomes unreachable-but-consistent instead of a contradiction with the 100k ceiling. Note the asymmetry this creates and decide it deliberately: `report_service._MAX_ROWS` stays 10000, so the fixed-10 path remains capped there, while the builder path honours the per-definition MaxRows. If the intent was actually to hard-cap ALL report generation at 10k for memory reasons, the cheaper and more honest fix is the opposite one: lower `le=100_000` to `le=10000` in both `schemas/report_builder.py:165` and `report_builder.py:239` and drop `MAX_ROWS_CEILING` to 10000, so the schema stops advertising a range that provably cannot execute. Verify with a test that executes a definition at `max_rows=10001` and asserts either success-with-10001-rows or a 400 at write time — not at render time.

findings.title: Successful builder executions never reach FINISHED; the reclaimer then rewrites a completed audit row to FAILED
findings.why_it_matters: Verified in source: `report_builder_tasks.py` writes status only at :83 (`task_row.status = "RUNNING"`) and :113 (`task_row.status = "FAILED"`). No code path writes `"FINISHED"`. Because `reclaim_stale_execution_logs` (pcs-backend/app/workers/report_tasks.py:263-308) selects rows whose status is in ('QUEUED','RUNNING') and older than the threshold, a builder execution that completed successfully and produced a report file is, 15 minutes later, relabelled FAILED with a `reclaimed_at` note in `condition_snapshot` -- on a table the module docstring calls an audit record that must not be tampered with. The polling endpoint therefore reports a failure for work that actually produced a file. (The reclaimer itself does not commit -- see the P0 -- so today this second corruption is masked; fixing the P0 without this fix turns the masked bug into a live one.)
evidence: pcs-backend/app/workers/report_builder_tasks.py:83 — `task_row.status = "RUNNING"` (only assignment in success path).
pcs-backend/app/workers/report_builder_tasks.py:113 — `task_row.status = "FAILED"` (only assignment in failure arm).
Search confirms no `task_row.status = "FINISHED"` exists anywhere in the file or in `report_builder.py` / `builder_service.py`.
Trigger: a successful execute_definition run returns report_file_id, user sees FINISHED; 15 min later reclaim rewrites the row to FAILED with no upstream signal.

pcs-backend/app/workers/report_builder_tasks.py:93-96 — `            file_id = await _render_and_store(` / `                db, out=out, project_id=pid, job_id=job_id, task_id=job_id,` / `                output_format=out.snapshot.get("output_format") or "pdf")` / `            await db.commit()` — the success path commits without ever setting `task_row.status = "FINISHED"`.

pcs-backend/app/workers/report_builder_tasks.py:112 — `            if attempt_no >= MAX_TRIES and task_row is not None:` — the only place `task_row.status` is assigned after the initial RUNNING, and it only ever assigns FAILED.

pcs-backend/app/api/v1/report_builder.py:296 — `    status = "FINISHED" if row.report_file_id else (row.status or "QUEUED")` — the DB column is never read as FINISHED, which is why the missing write is invisible.

pcs-backend/app/workers/report_tasks.py:284-285 — `            ReportExecutionLog.status.in_(("QUEUED", "RUNNING")),` / `            or_(ReportExecutionLog.updated_at < cutoff,` — the reclaim predicate a completed (still RUNNING) row satisfies.
pcs-backend/app/models/report.py:211 — comment="QUEUED 已入队 / RUNNING 执行中 / FINISHED 已出文件 / FAILED 已终结（含被回收）" — FINISHED is a defined terminal state that is never produced.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `task_row.status = "FINISHED"` after the successful `db.commit()` in `execute_definition_task` and before the final return; second commit. Alternative: set `status = "FINISHED"` together with `report_file_id` via the same UPDATE in `_link_report_file`. Either fix also removes the need for the heuristic `report_file_id is not None -> FINISHED` fallback in `execution_status` (which itself is a sign the underlying state machine is broken).

findings.title: Poll loop has no cancellation token: unmount or a new run resurrects an orphan loop that clobbers the new run's state
findings.why_it_matters: Verified in source. `poll(id)` (:151-179) re-arms itself with `poll(id)` at the end of its async callback and writes into a single shared `timer` ref; `stopPolling` (:86-88) only clears whatever is currently in that ref. `run()` calls `stopPolling()` (:121) then starts a new `poll(accepted.task_id)` -- but if the previous run's callback is already awaiting `reportBuilderApi.executionStatus`, it resumes afterwards, sets `statusText`, and calls `poll(oldId)` again, taking over `timer.current`. The page then has two live loops, and whichever resolves last wins `fileId`, so a download button can point at the previous run's file. The unmount cleanup `useEffect(() => stopPolling, [])` (:89) has the same hole: unmounting while a status request is in flight lets that callback re-arm a timer for a component that is gone. Both defects are the same missing generation guard and share one fix. The reviewer cited two separate lines; they merge.

No new dependency or state machine needed.

findings.title: Polling loop never reads the terminal FAILED status and spins until a false timeout
findings.why_it_matters: Verified in source: `poll` (:151-179) only tests `st.report_file_id`; it never looks at `st.status`. `ReportExecutionStatus` was given a real `status` column by migration p8_007 precisely so a failed execution is distinguishable from a running one, and the backend writes FAILED at pcs-backend/app/workers/report_builder_tasks.py:113. The frontend therefore keeps polling a job that has already failed, for the full `POLL_TIMEOUT_MS` (:60), and then shows the timeout message -- which asserts the file may still be generating. That is the exact false conclusion the p8_007 docstring was written to prevent.
